correctness.rationale: For every n≥r≥1, the proof first bounds online depth by the number of distinct windows (m or m+1) and by the size r of every positive query fiber. A proven prefix-threshold lemma on blocks of at most r consecutive window starts supplies matching complete mistake trees. The null branch induction is carried out for 2^h−1 consecutive starts plus the empty concept. For static shattering, 101 is forbidden on any triple, and four binary pair labels are characterized explicitly, then counted by inclusion-exclusion. Edge cases r=1 and m=1 are included. A separate defining-recursion checker passed on 272 rank classes (n≤16) and exact trace coefficients for n≤14; enumeration corroborates but does not prove all-parameter identities.

evidence: Alon–Beimel–Moran–Stemmer (2020), PMLR 125, covers closure properties and bounds on online dimensions of concept classes, rather than exact finite window ranks.
Ghazi–Golowich–Kumar–Manurangsi (2021), PMLR 132, improves closure bounds, without giving these fixed-width coefficients.
Malliaris–Moran (2021), arXiv:2108.05569, develops stability and online learning, but no claimed exact finite-window formula.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Known generic cardinality bounds and interval-class results constrain the dimensions but do not imply equality at both numerical caps. The window positive-fiber cap r, block-threshold lower construction, and the effect of adding one null hypothesis are used essentially.

value.rationale: The natural problem is point-membership identification of an equal-length sliding interval with or without a null state. The result simultaneously classifies its exact adaptive and static shattering across every ground-set size, gives a sharp power-of-two boundary at which one null hypothesis increases online rank, and exhibits an unbounded VC=1 versus Littlestone gap along n=2r. The exact null-state transition and paired shattering polynomials are structural facts not merely a numerical gain or a fixed-size census.
